nodes.name: Pyrolysis of core-shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67
nodes.procedure: core-shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 pyrolyzed to generate hollow polyhedral porous carbon with Co nanoparticle supported (Co_n@NPC), where the evaporated Zn in ZIF-8 isolates contiguous Co atoms to form uniform Co crystal during the pyrolysis process (Figure S15-17). Meanwhile, N-pointed cavities are created by Zn evaporation and Co aggregation. The appropriate pyrolysis temperature (Figure S35-36), pyrolysis time (Figure S37-38), and Co/Zn mole ratio (Figure S39-41) are necessary for the uniform growth of Co nanoparticles.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, we chose core-shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67[16] as a precursor (Figure S9-S14) to generate hollow polyhedral porous carbon with Co nanoparticle supported (Co_n@NPC) , where the evaporated Zn in ZIF-8 isolates contiguous Co atoms to form uniform Co crystal during the pyrolysis process (Figure S15-17)

nodes.name: Pt impregnation and confinement
nodes.procedure: Co_n@NPC was impregnated in an H2PtCl6 solution to capture free [PtCl6]2- ions, accompanied by confining Pt atoms in N-pointed cavities through Pt-N coordination at 60°C. The facile low-temperature treatment avoids the accumulation of Pt atoms, and the design of the core-shell structure also protects Pt1 from dissolution. Additionally, driven by the difference in reduction potentials between the Co and Pt ions, galvanic replacement reaction occurs simultaneously. The Co_n was oxidized and dissolved into the solution while Pt ions were reduced.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 4a, Co_n-Pt_1@NPC shows a higher HER performance than Pt_1@NPC and commercial Pt/C in alkaline. It only requires an overpotential of 20 mV to achieve a geometric current density of -10 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀)... the Tafel slope of Co_n-Pt_1@NPC is 29.07 mV·dec⁻¹ in alkaline... Even at 100 mA cm⁻², the overpotential of Co_n-Pt_1@NPC (91 mV) in alkali is only half that of Pt/C (178 mV)... Co_n-Pt_1@NPC shows no obvious decay after a long period of 100 h in alkaline... exhibits the highest turnover frequency (TOF), mass activity, and intrinsic HER activity

nodes.characterization_summary: Co nanoparticle diameter reduced from ~26 nm in Co_n@NPC to ~16 nm in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC. Size-tunable Co nanoparticles from 9.8 nm to 23.3 nm by regulating Co/Zn ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diameter of Co_n in Co_n@NPC is reduced from ∼26 nm (Figure S19) to ∼16 nm in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC from ZIF-8@ZIF-67 precursor with a Co/Zn ratio of 1/1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Individual Pt atoms coexist with Co nanoparticles (yellow circles). Clear lattice fringe of 0.175 nm assigned to Co(200) plane, implying Pt not inserted into Co lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2j demonstrates that Pt atoms mainly fall on the carbon surface. Moreover, the lattice fringes of Co_n remain unchanged after Pt introduction, showing a clear lattice fringe of 0.175 nm assigned to the (200) plane...

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomically dispersed Pt sites homogeneously surround Co_n.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-coupled EDS element mapping also reveals that the atomically dispersed Pt sites homogeneously surround Co_n (Figure 2l and Figure S25).

nodes.characterization_summary: No diffraction associated with bulk Pt whereas Co crystal diffractions are resolved.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Exactly, there is no diffraction associated with bulk Pt whereas Co crystal diffractions are resolved on X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 2m and Figure S26).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f deconvoluted to Pt²⁺/Pt⁴⁺ (no Pt⁰). Pt²⁺ shifts -0.30 eV in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC vs Pt_1@NPC (electron accumulation). Co 2p (Co-Nx, metallic Co) shifts to higher BE vs Co_n@NPC (electron transfer Co→Pt). N 1s metal-N proportion increases after Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Pt_1@NPC free of Co_n, a negative shift of 0.30 eV is observed on Pt²⁺ in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC, suggesting the electron accumulation on Pt_1... Co-Nx and metallic Co peaks positively shift to higher binding energy...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows oxidation state between Pt foil and PtO2, consistent with XPS. Co K-edge XANES reflects dominant metallic properties of Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed in Pt L3 edge XANES spectra, Pt in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC shows an oxidation state between Pt foil and PtO2 (Figure 3d), consistent with XPS results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge FT: peak 1.60 Å (Pt-C/N), no Pt-Pt (2.54 Å), Pt-O (1.67 Å), Pt-Co (2.2 Å). Fitting: Pt-N 2.01 Å, CN=3.9. Co K-edge FT: Co-Co 2.08 Å, CN=5.5 (moderate Co_n size).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co_n-Pt_1@NPC displays a prominent peak at 1.60Å originating from the Pt-C/N vector... no Pt-Pt (2.54Å) and Pt-O (1.67Å) vectors are observed. The peak at R = 2.2Å for Pt-Co backscattering is also not found...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 408, 578, 752, 1000 cm⁻¹ attributed to Co-OH species decrease with increased potential. Pt-H peak at 2100 cm⁻¹ and C-H at 2800-3100 cm⁻¹ strengthen with potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Four obvious Raman bands centered at 408, 578, 752, and 1000 cm⁻¹ are observed at the beginning of the applied potential, attributed to Co-OH species, and their intensities gradually decrease with the increased scanning time.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt content 6.47 wt% in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC (vs 4.16 wt% in Co_n+c-Pt_1@NPC).
nodes.evidence_snippet: higher Pt contents in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC (6.47%) than that in Co_n+c-Pt_1@NPC (4.16 wt%) also indicate that the volatilization of Zn does provide confined spaces for Pt sites (Table S4).
